Julius Caesar, stabbed by senators on the Ides of March in 44 BC, falls at the foot of the statue of his old rival Pompey. Victor Honoré Janssens, a Flemish painter, painted this version of the assassination around 1700.

The emperor Charlemagne and his son Louis the Pious stand side by side in a manuscript illumination from a French royal chronicle of the 1300s or 1400s. Louis became emperor after Charlemagne died in 814.
